clue.text: Most recent example of capital gains for Americans

definitions.text: Most recent example of capital gains for Americans

parts.words: Most recent example of capital gains for Americans
parts.note: read not as money made on investments but as the newest state capital the USA acquired, when Hawaii joined the union in 1959

explanation.surface: A remark about the latest tax treatment of investment profits in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital gains' wants to be the tax term; here it means a capital city gained. Hawaii was the last state admitted, so its capital is the latest one Americans picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii, the fiftieth and most recently admitted American state.

clue.text: Criticism feared by high-fliers?

definitions.meaning: anti-aircraft fire, which pilots flying high over enemy ground dread

explanation.surface: Ambitious high achievers dread being criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-fliers' suggests ambitious people, but the second sense is literal airmen. One of the themed entries: its letters split into the state codes FL and AK.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is slang for criticism and also, originally, the German term for anti-aircraft guns and their fire.

clue.text: Limited edition is about great inventor

parts.note: edition cut short, its usual abbreviation ED
taken as written
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A small print run of a book is about a famous inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited edition' looks like a collector's item; here 'limited' just shortens the word to ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Writer of religious works composed missal, in part

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who writes sacred texts put together part of a prayer book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' reads as writing music or text; it is the anagram signal for MISSAL plus PT. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalmist is a composer of psalms, the sacred songs of the Bible's Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Reprimanded actors I had placed around entrance

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a production

indicators.note: the first piece is put round the outside of the second, so one wraps the other

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, written ID
a gate is an entrance to a field or garden

explanation.surface: Performers were told off after a scene at a stage door.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke or criticise severely, so castigated means reprimanded.

clue.text: Poet who died at Florence — from England, originally

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the answer is lifted from inside the following words

explanation.surface: A biographical note on an English-born poet who died in Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from England, originally' reads as a biographical aside, true of the poet, but it holds him in its letters. A themed entry: LA, ND and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Savage Landor was an English poet and writer who died in Florence in 1864.

clue.text: Native worker welcoming chief executive and president

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: coolie was an old, now offensive, word for an unskilled native labourer in Asia
DG stands for director-general, the chief executive of an organisation

explanation.surface: A local labourer greets the company boss and the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief executive and president' reads as one person; 'and' is a link, with 'president' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin Coolidge was the thirtieth President of the United States, serving 1923 to 1929.

clue.text: It fills men crazed with acrimony, ultimately

definitions.text: It fills men crazed with acrimony, ultimately

indicators.note: fills means goes into the middle of, so these two letters sit inside the rest
crazed means driven wild, so these letters are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bitterness drives deranged men to hostility in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazed' makes ENM from MEN, and 'ultimately' adds Y from acrimony; IT 'fills' them as ENM-IT-Y. The whole clue also describes hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is deep hostility or hatred, the feeling that fills men driven mad with bitterness.

clue.text: Mark covering a learner producing quantity, but lacking direction

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round something, so the first piece goes outside the other

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
L for learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: A blemish on a student driver gives an aimless quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link. This is one of the entries listed at 15 across, its letters splitting into three state postal codes.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a scalar has magnitude only, unlike a vector, which also has direction.

clue.text: Explorer as pioneer in tourist industry

definitions.meaning: Captain James ..., the eighteenth-century British navigator who charted the Pacific
Thomas ..., the Victorian who founded the package-tour business

explanation.surface: A traveller of old described as a founder of the holiday trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Two famous Cooks: James the navigator and Thomas the travel agent. A themed entry: its letters split into the state codes CO and OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook explored the Pacific, while Thomas Cook invented the organised excursion and the travel agency.

clue.text: Lack of distinction limited us, I recollected

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered again in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remembers that a failure to tell things apart held them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering; read it as collected again, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Similitude is likeness or resemblance, a state where two things cannot be told apart.

clue.text: Advertise in flier

parts.note: to puff something is to promote it with exaggerated praise
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to promote something in a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' wants to be a printed handbill; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a seabird, so a flier, with a striking coloured beak.

clue.text: It's not true about resistance being caused by abrasiveness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: fictional means invented, not true
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Denying a claim that resistance arises from roughness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'being' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Frictional describes what friction does, the resistance produced by surfaces rubbing together.

clue.text: Sets off a short time before construction workers

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next in the answer

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
riggers erect scaffolding and lifting gear on building sites

explanation.surface: Something starts a moment ahead of the building crew arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or cause it to start, as a gun's trigger fires it.

clue.text: 2, 6, 9, 10, 21, 24 across, 24 down, 25 — plus 30 others

parts.note: the listed entries each split into two-letter postal codes of American ..., twenty in all; thirty more make up the full federal union

explanation.surface: A cross-reference listing several entries plus thirty more.
explanation.walkthrough: FLAK is FL+AK, LANDOR LA+ND+OR, SCALAR SC+AL+AR, COOK CO+OK, GAMINE GA+MI+NE, WINY WI+NY, WAIL WA+IL, INVADE IN+VA+DE: twenty state codes, and with thirty others the fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: The country comprises fifty states, twenty of which are coded in the listed entries.

clue.text: Respected opponents at bridge fell heavily

parts.note: in bridge East and South sit in rival partnerships, so E and S are opponents
rain that teemed down fell heavily

explanation.surface: Card players who were held in high regard took a heavy tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell heavily' suggests a hard fall; it is rain pouring down.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to respect and admire them, so esteemed means respected.

clue.text: See 15
Poles carrying quantity of fish to Pennsylvania city

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: S and N, the south and north poles
a cran is a measure of fresh herrings, about 750 fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people carry a catch of fish to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' wants to be people from Poland; it means the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Scranton is a city in north-eastern Pennsylvania, once a centre of coal mining.

clue.text: Under pressure, get in touch with advocate

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to reach someone is to contact them

explanation.surface: A stressed person is urged to contact a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advocate' looks like a noun, a lawyer; it is the verb, to urge or recommend.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach a course of action is to advocate it earnestly.

clue.text: A soldier and sailor going across to troublemaker

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: the sailor's letters span the little word, so one goes outside the other

parts.note: a tar is an old name for a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier and a seaman head over to a rabble-rouser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link: TAR straddles TO to make TATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up public unrest, a political troublemaker.

clue.text: Charming girl willing to do things around home

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: game means up for it, willing
in means at home

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman happy to help out at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed entry: its letters split into the state codes GA, MI and NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim, elfin girl with an appealing mischievous charm.

clue.text: They grow up in Lebanon, badly scared

indicators.note: badly means in a damaged or wrong way, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Children raised in war-torn Lebanon are badly frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They grow up' suggests children; it means trees growing tall.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar of Lebanon is the country's famous native tree, appearing on its flag.

clue.text: Keen to include her fruit for pie

indicators.note: to include means holding within, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eager to add her favourite fruit to the pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb for lamenting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherries are a fruit commonly baked in pies, as in cherry pie.

clue.text: Speed on one motorway way too high

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece listed comes last

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M marks a British motorway, as in the M1
a mode is a way of doing something
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Driving on a motorway far too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'way' is the trick: the first belongs to 'motorway', the second is MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoderate means excessive, going beyond reasonable limits, as prices too high.

clue.text: Audibly complaining it's tasting like something fermented

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the answer sounds like the word for moaning

parts.note: whiny means habitually complaining

explanation.surface: Someone moans that their drink has gone sour.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed entry: its letters split into the state codes WI and NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Winy describes a taste or smell like wine, which is fermented grape juice.

clue.text: Breaking rule, I brought up complaint

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up reads the letters from the bottom upwards
breaking means splitting open, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Someone who broke the rules is told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' puts I inside the rule, 'brought up' turns the whole result in this down entry. One of the entries listed at 15 across: two state postal codes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wail is a long cry of grief or protest, so a complaint.

clue.text: Attacked with words, we hear — and attack with force

indicators.note: we hear means the clue word is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: to inveigh is to attack with angry words

explanation.surface: Verbal attacks followed by physical ones.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed entry: its letters split into the state codes IN, VA and DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To invade is to enter a country or place with armed force.

clue.text: President Ford, as seen in movies

definitions.meaning: Benjamin or William Henry ..., both Presidents of the United States
the film star surnamed Ford, of Star Wars and Indiana Jones

explanation.surface: Gerald Ford appears on the big screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Ford' reads as Gerald Ford; split it: one president, and the actor Ford's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Harrisons were US Presidents, and the actor Harrison Ford stars in many films.
